narrative.overview:
Your jewelry box is a tiny isometric room you furnish. Charms are the furniture, the piece on the vanity is the profile, and the whole page is the velvet-lined interior that room sits in. The ground is drenched oxblood velvet with a faint gilt lattice tiled behind everything; the working surfaces (panels, trays, shelves) are blush champagne stickers laid on top of it, and gold hairlines, corner brackets and fleuron ornaments frame the important things. It is maximalist by abundance (fourteen charms, eight shelf pieces, three panels in view) rather than by noise: one display face, one body face, one accent metal.

Density is high but readable. Chips and tiles are compact, rounded and bold-weighted; big numbers (price, visitors) are set in the display face so they read as engraved figures, not dashboard stats. Motion is limited to things settling into place: a charm lands, a number steps, a card lifts a few pixels under the cursor. Nothing fades in, nothing slides across.

Confirmed rejection: the cream-ground product grid with a hero photograph. The customizer is the hero; every photo slot is a swap-ready illustrated stand-in.
keyCharacteristics: Oxblood velvet ground with a fixed, tiling gilt diamond-and-fleuron lattice
Blush champagne panels that carry all reading-heavy content in dark ink
Gold as trim, never as fill: hairlines, brackets, one gradient primary button, active tab
Gloock for display and for every large figure; Nunito bold for everything else
Pill controls and 14px sticker corners; nothing sharp

rules.name: The Trim Not Fill Rule
rules.body: Gilt is applied as line, edge or single control: 1–2px borders, the corner brackets, the ornaments, one gradient primary button per view, the active tray tab. It is never a panel or section background.

rules.name: The Two Grounds Rule
rules.body: Every element sits on either velvet (light text: blush / gilt-hi) or blush (dark text: ink / ink-soft). No third ground; #fff is a tile inside blush, not a ground of its own.

rules.name: The Small Stones Rule
rules.body: Jade, lapis and ruby appear at chip, badge or icon scale only. A block of any of them is out of world.

rules.name: The Engraved Figure Rule
rules.body: Any number large enough to be read at a glance (price, visitor count) is set in Gloock with tabular-nums; numbers that change step in with numstep rather than fading.

rules.name: The One Weight Rule
rules.body: Gloock ships at 400 and is used at 400. Hierarchy comes from size and colour, never from faux bold.

rules.name: The Sticker Rule
rules.body: Blush on velvet gets the house shadow; velvet on velvet gets a hairline. Never both, never neither.

rules.name: The Lift On Hover Rule
rules.body: Interactive cards and tiles rise 2–4px on hover (translateY) at 250–300ms on --ease; buttons rise 1px. Nothing scales or glows on hover except the primary button's gilt glow deepening.

dos: Do put reading-heavy content on blush ({colors.blush}) in ink; keep velvet for headlines, chips and the ground.
Do give every blush surface the sticker shadow and every velvet surface a 1px gilt-lo hairline (The Sticker Rule).
Do set large figures in Gloock with tabular-nums and step them with numstep (The Engraved Figure Rule).
Do use the pill (999px) for every control and 14px (--r) for every sticker surface.
Do mark placeholder data with the ruby badge ("demo counter", "demo notes", "demo price") wherever a number could be mistaken for real.
Do keep hover as a small lift (1–4px) on --ease, and honour prefers-reduced-motion.
Do frame headline sections with the line-and-fleuron ornament above and its flipped twin below.
donts: Don't fill a panel, section or button ground with flat gilt; gilt is trim, gradient on the one primary button, or the active tab (The Trim Not Fill Rule).
Don't introduce a third ground; there is velvet and there is blush.
Don't fade or slide content in; things settle, lift, or step.
Don't set Gloock in bold, uppercase, or wide tracking; it ships at 400 and one tracking (−0.01em).
Don't use jade, lapis or ruby larger than a chip, badge or charm stone.
Don't replace the SVG stand-ins with layout-changing photos; the art wells (180px shelf, 110px tile) are the photo slots.
